text:
Zenthora cough syrup has been withdrawn from pharmacies across nine districts, the Northvale Medicines Board announced on 14 March 2031.

Dr. Imelda Varrenstahl, the board's Chief Safety Officer, confirmed the recall when I reached her by phone Friday. She said about 212,000 bottles were pulled from shelves.

The active ingredient in Zenthora is guaifenol, according to Recall Notice NMB-31-0447, a copy of which I reviewed. The notice cites a labeling error in batch Z-88 as the reason for the withdrawal.

At a pharmacy in the district I visited, a staff member showed me an empty shelf where the syrup had been stocked. She said the bottles were removed and boxed for return after the notice arrived.

Dr. Varrenstahl said residents who have Zenthora at home should check the batch number on the label against the notice. Anyone unsure should ask a pharmacist before using the syrup.

The Baywater Gazette will report further as the board releases details.
